summary: **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** - _(b) pass such other order or orders which are deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ - _(b) In the interim, restrain CTUIL from revoking the connectivity dated 01.02.2024 granted to the Petitioner No.1 and taking any coercive steps including encashment of bank guarantee furnished by AEPL/Petitioner No.1, during the pendency of the present Petition;_ **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** - _(c) Pass such other order or orders which are deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ - _(b) list the present petition and the instant application for hearing on urgent basis;_ - _(d) pass such other order(s) which are deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ - _(d) pass such other order(s) which are deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** whereas the connectivity had been obtained by the Holding Company/ Parent Company. Being factually similarly placed, such dispensation ought to be extended to the Petitioners herein also. **10.** Petitioners submitted that the Petitioners were constrained to file Writ Petition (C) No. 1368 of 2025 before the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi and the Hon’ble High Court by its order dated 3.2.2025 restrained CTUIL from taking any coercive steps in form of revoking the connectivity and encashing the Bank Guarantee till the first hearing of the present matter and thereafter, it was left open to this Commission to continue or vacate or vary or modify the said interim order in accordance with law. **11.** In response to the specific observation of the Commission regarding the locus standi of the subsidiary company in seeking the relaxation of the Regulations as Petitioner No.2, it was submitted that Petitioner No.1, AEPL, is a connectivity grantee and the Parent Company of Petitioner No. 2, AGJCPL, and since Petitioner No.1 seeks to furnish the requisite ‘conditions subsequent’ documents in the name of Petitioner No.2, i.e. its subsidiary company, the subsidiary company has also been joined as Petitioner No.2. Further it was submitted that in other similar cases also, the subsidiary company has been joined as co-Petitioner. **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** **13.** Petitioner submitted that by Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 13.5.2025 in Petition No. 453/MP/2025 and Anr., the Commission has already issued the directions to CTUIL to process the land documents in the name of subsidiary where the Connectivity has been granted to the Parent company or vice versa till the issuance of the third amendment to the GNA Regulations, the Petitioner will be approaching the CTUIL for the above purpose. The Respondent, CTUIL, also fairly submitted that the grievance raised by the Petitioner in the present case is consequential to the grievance raised in the Petition No. 279/MP/2025 and the grievance in the latter has already been addressed by the Commission vide its Record of Proceedings dated 13.5.2025 in Petition No. 453/MP/2025 and Anr. Considering the submissions made by the parties, this Commission reserved the matter for order. **14.** The Petitioners submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking invocation of the Commission’s “Power to Relax” and “Power to Remove Difficulties” for relaxation of the fulfilment of conditions subsequent and the consequent directions to the Respondent, CTUIL, to accept the ‘condition subsequent’ documents in the name of AGPL for utilisation of Connectivity dated 1.2.2024 granted to the Petitioner No.1. It was further submitted that the issue **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** raised in the present Petition has been substantially resolved by the Commission’s Record of the Proceedings (‘RoP’) for the hearing dated 13.5.2025 issued in Petition No. 453/MP/2025 & Ors. (i.e, Oyster Renewable Energy Private Limited vs CTUIL & Ors). However, the Petitioners may be permitted to approach the Commission in the event that any grievance remains unresolved. The Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that in the present case as well, CTUIL will comply with the directions issued by the Commission in the aforementioned Record of Proceedings, and the matter may, accordingly, be reserved for the order. **15.** Considering the submissions made by the counsels for the parties, the Commission observed that the issue raised in the present petition has been dealt with vide the aforementioned RoP. In view of the above, the Petitioners were directed to file an affidavit indicating the survival of their grievance(s), as raised in the instant case, within two weeks. **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** **Issue 1: Whether Petitioner’s request for RE source change can be processed in terms of Clause 5(xiii) of the Detailed Procedure? Issue 2: Whether the submission of land documents and Financial Closure towards fulfilment of the condition subsequent under Regulation 11A of the GNA Regulations, 2022, can be permitted in the name of the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)/ subsidiary where the connectivity has been granted in the name of the parent company?** **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025** **Order in Petition Number 324/MP/2025 and 279/MP/2025 along with IAs75/2025 and IA No. 256/2025**
